# Decay constants from noisy detector traces

You are given afterglow traces in `/app/data/traces.csv` (columns `trace_id,t_s,counts`).
Each trace follows a single exponential decay plus a constant background, with occasional one-sided spikes.

## Deliverable
Write `/app/output/rates.csv` with columns `trace_id,rate_per_s`, one row per trace.

## Evaluation
| metric | pass if |
|---|---|
| `median_rel_error` | ≤ 0.05 |
| `p90_rel_error` | ≤ 0.12 |

The baseline counting rate is measured in a separate patch of the detector.
synthetic-prog:
# Fragment length from strand-shift profiles

Mapped single-end reads are in `/app/data/reads/*.tagAlign.gz` (BED6). Estimate each library's mean fragment length.

## Deliverables
1. `/app/output/fragments.csv` with `sample_id,fragment_bp`.
2. A program `/app/output/solution_cli.py` run as `python /app/output/solution_cli.py <input_dir> <output_dir>` on unseen batches.

## Evaluation
Hidden batches have a different read length. `hidden_mae_bp` must be ≤ 12 and `public_mae_bp` ≤ 10.

# Glass content of powders by internal-standard XRD

A baseline-free localisation is not required here. Fit the background level of each pattern, patch by patch,
and report the amorphous fraction. The naive Rietveld refinement of the crystalline phases is not enough.

Report `/app/output/glass.csv` with `sample,glass_wt_pct`; pass if `rmse_wt_pct` ≤ 2.5.
